input.name: image
input.layout: NCHW: [batch, channel, row, column], rows top to bottom
input.content: One flattened patch: a square of the surface exactly one tile period on a side, upright, starting anywhere within the tile pattern. Made by the flatten step below.

output.name: logits
output.content: One number per message bit. logits[0][i] belongs to Message index i of /docs/message-format.md. Bit i is 1 when the number is greater than 0, else 0.

flatten.input: the camera frame as RGB, and four corners in frame pixels
flatten.coordinates: x to the right, y down, in pixels of the image. The top-left corner of the image is (0, 0) and the centre of the pixel in column j, row i is (j + 0.5, i + 0.5).
flatten.mapping: Find the homography H (3x3, perspective) that takes the four target_corners to the four frame corners, in the order listed. For the output pixel in column j, row i, compute (u, v, w) = H * (j + 0.5, i + 0.5, 1) and read the frame at (x, y) = (u / w, v / w).
flatten.interpolation_detail: Blend the four frame pixels whose centres surround (x, y): with fx = x - 0.5 and fy = y - 0.5, the columns are floor(fx) and floor(fx) + 1 with weights 1 - frac(fx) and frac(fx), and the same for rows. No smoothing or mipmapping before sampling.
flatten.outside_frame: pixels outside the frame count as 0 (black)
flatten.colour: no colour conversion; sample the 8-bit RGB values as they are
flatten.output: float values; divide by 255 to get the reader input. In use, do not round. When checking against a fixture, round to whole 8-bit levels first: the expected logits come from the 8-bit patch.

camera.px_per_tile_means: camera pixels across one printed tile (one tile period), seen straight on

starting_band.note: where training starts; the trained code is free to sit elsewhere

reading.frames_averaged_means: average the reader's logits over the last 3 frames of one scan, then read the bits
reading.scan_distance_means: phone to print; the trained camera range (camera.trained_px_per_tile) is this distance on the measured phone

bits.order: index i is Message index i in /docs/message-format.md
bits.decoding: error correction and checksum are not part of the models; see /docs/message-format.md

fixtures.expected_values_from: PyTorch, reading <name>_patch.png as 8-bit RGB divided by 255
fixtures.compare: the logits, not only the bits; /docs/model-contract.md says how closely
fixtures.frames_from: generated images put through the training simulation; no camera, no dataset
fixtures.frame_is: a portrait window onto the surface at TILE_PX pixels per tile, in the 9:16 shape of the camera stream but not at its size; a real frame is camera.stream_px

verification.what: each ONNX file run in ONNX Runtime (CPU) against PyTorch (CPU, float32) on the same inputs
